title: Father! I Wait Thy Word. the Sun Doth Stand
description: Father! I Wait Thy Word. the Sun Doth Stand in Tonic Solfa to PENITENTIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Jones Very wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 268, “The Son”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PENITENTIA; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther! I wait Thy word. The sun doth stand Be-neath the min-gling line of night and day, A lis-tening ser-vant, wait-ing Thy com-mand, To roll re-joic-ing on its si-lent way.

lines: Father! I wait Thy word. The sun doth stand
Beneath the mingling line of night and day,
A listening servant, waiting Thy command,
To roll rejoicing on its silent way.
The tongue of time abides the appointed hour,
Till on our ear its solemn warnings fall;
The heavy cloud withholds the pelting shower, —
Then, every drop speeds onward at Thy call.
The bird reposes on the yielding bough,
With breast unswollen by the tide of song; —
So does my spirit wait Thy presence now,
To pour Thy praise in quickening life along.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Jones Very died in 1880.
credits: Words by Jones Very (1813–1880), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to PENITENTIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
